request.system:
You are the Extractor agent in a newsroom verification pipeline. You read one SEC filing
document and record what the employer itself says about job cuts and AI. You record claims only.
You never infer causation, never paraphrase quotes and never use a reporter's or analyst's framing.

Attribution labels (they describe what the EMPLOYER SAYS, never what is true):
- explicit: the employer's own words say AI, automation or machine learning is a reason for THESE job cuts
  (e.g. "we are reducing roles as AI now handles this work").
- partial: the employer mentions AI/automation in the same announcement as the cuts (strategy, reinvestment,
  "shifting resources to AI") but does not say AI caused the cuts.
- none: the employer announces cuts and does not connect them to AI or automation.

Return ONE JSON object with exactly these keys:
{
  "is_workforce_reduction": true | false,      // does the document announce job cuts / layoffs / a reduction in force?
  "company": string,                          // the employer's name as written in the document
  "event_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | null,          // date of the announcement or of the cuts, if stated
  "jobs_cut": integer | null,                 // number of positions cut, ONLY if the document states a number
  "jobs_cut_text": string | null,             // the exact words stating the number or percentage, copied verbatim
  "cut_quote": string | null,                 // the one sentence, copied VERBATIM, in which the document announces or
                                              // reports the job cuts; null when is_workforce_reduction is false
  "ai_attribution": "explicit" | "partial" | "none",
  "ai_quote": string | null,                  // 1-2 sentences copied VERBATIM (character for character) in which the
                                              // employer connects the cuts to AI/automation; null when attribution is none
  "notes": string                             // one short sentence on anything ambiguous
}
is_workforce_reduction is true ONLY when the document itself announces or reports job cuts. Mentions inside
forward-looking-statement disclaimers, risk-factor lists or legal boilerplate (e.g. "the effectiveness of our
restructuring and workforce reduction program", "artificial intelligence laws") do NOT count, and an AI quote must never
come from that boilerplate.
Copy quotes exactly as they appear, including punctuation. If the document states a percentage but no headcount,
set jobs_cut to null and put the percentage wording in jobs_cut_text. Output JSON only.
request.user:
Company (from SEC index): SOFTCAT PLC
Form / document type: UK RNS / UK announcement: Preliminary Results
Filed: 2026-10-14
Source URL: https://data.fca.org.uk/artefacts/NSM/RNS/43425248-2a27-4e79-9589-660c065bacbd.html

Document excerpt (paragraphs that mention staffing, restructuring, AI or automation):
<<<
AI is one of several factors making IT infrastructure more critical, complex and strategically important for our customers’ operations. While applications evolve and embed AI functionality, infrastructure foundations are being developed to cope with the rise in demand for compute, storage, faster and more resilient networks, better data architecture, greater security and stronger governance. At the same time, memory chip supply constraints have added complexity to pricing, availability and planning. This is exactly the sort of environment in which Softcat’s strengths shine brightest. Customers remain disciplined with their investments, but they continue to spend on technology, and they need our advice, technical capability, vendor reach and proven execution capabilities more than ever.

Post year-end, we announced the acquisition of GDT[3], a leading US-based multi-vendor IT solutions provider. This is a significant strategic step for Softcat, giving us enhanced capability in the US and strengthening our ability to serve customers with international requirements. GDT will strengthen our foundations for long-term growth, alongside and in combination with, our existing UK and Ireland business. We are very encouraged by how well received the transaction has been by customers, vendors and employees alike.

Our outstanding performance in FY2026 significantly exceeded our expectations at the beginning of the year. Softcat’s continued success reflects the strength of our special culture, the depth of our customer relationships and the benefits of sustained investment in our people, capabilities, systems, data and office network. Our proposition spans the full stack of modern infrastructure and is increasingly aligned to the technologies customers need most as they prepare for AI adoption at scale. We remain focused on enhancing our offering within a disciplined strategic framework, while continuing to invest in the capabilities, tools and operating model required to capture the significant long-term opportunity ahead.

AI is manifesting in very positive ways across our business. As it becomes more deeply embedded in the applications used by organisations every day, it is placing greater demands on the infrastructure layer where our offering is focused. Customers need more powerful and versatile compute, faster and lower-latency storage, more resilient networking and connectivity, stronger cyber security, and data architecture and governance capable of supporting AI safely and at scale. The market remains in the early stages of this adoption cycle, and we are very well positioned to benefit given the breadth and depth of our offering, the scale and diversity of our customer base, and our trusted adviser status with both customers and vendors.

Our market continues to be influenced by geopolitical uncertainty and industry-wide supply challenges for memory and storage products, driven by unprecedented AI infrastructure investment. Against this backdrop, customers remain disciplined and selective, with greater scrutiny of discretionary projects and a continued focus on demonstrable business outcomes and return on investment. However, IT infrastructure is becoming ever more foundational to organisational resilience and growth, and demand remains strong in areas that are difficult to defer, including security, hybrid infrastructure, networking, cloud optimisation, data platforms, AI enablement and managed services. While uncertainty around memory pricing persists, our close relationships with a range of key vendors help us advise customers, identify alternatives and provide flexible solutions.

We have also been modernising our own systems, data and digital platforms for several years with investments in data architecture, automation and AI-enabled tools beginning to enhance the way our people work. Alongside this, we are developing in-house agents across key processes and adopting AI functionality within our enterprise systems. These investments are improving customer and employee experience, increasing the effectiveness of our go-to-market activity, and strengthening the scalability of our business as we continue to grow.

AI and other factors continue to stimulate demand across our entire technology proposition, and there is broad recognition from customers that their infrastructure estates must evolve at pace. These environments are often highly complex, built over many years across a large number of different vendor’s technologies, which makes trusted, independent advice and support increasingly important. Softcat is very well placed in this environment, combining access to leading vendor innovation with a deep understanding of customer environments to help organisations plan, implement and integrate technology fit for the age of AI.

The broadest offering – our five technology towers continue to help customers, vendors and our own people navigate the full stack of modern infrastructure. We saw broad-based growth across the portfolio during the year, with particularly strong demand in data centre infrastructure, networking and security, workplace, and services. The 2025 acquisition of Oakland enhanced our capabilities in data, automation and AI consulting, enabling us to engage earlier with customers as they build the foundations required for AI adoption at scale. We will continue to develop technical skills and service capability across each tower to deepen our proposition and extend our reach, in close alignment with our vendor framework.

Operational excellence – we have made significant progress in modernising the systems, data and processes that will support Softcat’s next stage of growth. Our developing data architecture and platforms, proprietary tools and in-house agents are beginning to bring cleaner internal data together with external insight on customers, markets and products. We have also continued to enhance eCAT and made good progress expanding it globally. We have completed the rollout of our new HR system, while our new sales system is currently being rolled out in phases across the sales team. Together, these platforms will enable greater automation, better experiences for customers and employees, and improved scalability across the business.

Our special culture – our culture remains the central foundation of Softcat’s success and continues to evolve as the business grows. We have invested in and developed local leadership teams in each of our offices to strengthen employee experience and maintain the transparency, recognition and feedback that underpin engagement and collaboration. Our FY2026 employee net promoter score increased slightly to 56 (FY2025: 55), while our employee engagement score rose to 91% (FY2025: 88%). We also continued our office upgrade programme, creating better environments for collaboration between our people, customers, vendors and partners. During FY2026, we marked the tenth anniversary of our stock market listing, and to recognise their significant contribution to Softcat and its success, all Softcat and Oakland employees were rewarded with a special, one-off, free share award.

During the year, we made further progress with our ongoing investments in internal systems, data and processes. We are now moving from foundation-building into deployment, adopting AI functionality as it becomes available within third-party platforms and developing proprietary tools that improve how our people work. This includes CatNav, our intuitive in-house assistant designed to help sales teams navigate the breadth of Softcat’s proposition, vendor relationships and pricing structures more quickly and effectively. We have also continued to develop eCAT, our online IT procurement platform, through direct integrations with vendor systems, an enhanced user experience and further international expansion into Germany, Singapore and Australia.

We grew average headcount by 10.8% year-on-year to 2,925 and have continued to focus our investment in people across technical, specialist and sales support roles, while also growing our internal IT and back-office functions, as we enhance our capability to go deeper with existing customers.

We have made good progress with the implementation of our new sales and HR systems. The new HR system has now been rolled out to all users, while the new sales system has completed user acceptance testing and pilot phases and is now live for an initial group of sales colleagues, ahead of a phased wider rollout. Together, these platforms will enable greater automation, better experiences for customers and employees, and more scalable processes across the Group.

Our outstanding FY2026 performance demonstrates the strength of our business model and the benefits of consistent strategic execution. We continued to support a diverse range of new and existing customers with their IT infrastructure requirements, drawing on our deep expertise, comprehensive product and services offering, and the exceptional service delivered by our highly engaged employees.

We are also benefitting from the recent investments we’ve made in systems and data, people and our office network. These investments have strengthened our capabilities, improved our internal operations and supported further market share gains and long-term sustainable growth. They also position us well to capture the benefits of AI, both within our own business and for customers, as more organisations move from experimentation to broader deployment.

Underlying operating cost growth was driven by increased commissions in line with commissionable GP growth and a 16.0% increase in wages and salaries. During the year, average headcount grew by 10.8% (7.7% year-on-year excluding Oakland), while closing headcount grew by 9.7% year-on-year (8.0% growth excluding Oakland). In addition to the annualised impact of the step up in Employers’ National Insurance Contributions, underlying operating costs also include significant investment in expanding our internal IT team and corporate development capability, investment in our data and digital strategy, and office refurbishment costs. In addition, several one-time items were also recognised in underlying operating costs, including the one-off free share award to employees, an overperformance element of variable pay and employee incentives, and advisory costs relating to the acquisition of GDT.

During the year, we have continued to invest in Softcat’s future growth by increasing headcount and building new capabilities, developing our data and digital platforms, investing in core systems, IT capability, and our office network. In addition, the Group completed its first ever share buyback programme totalling £45.0m in February 2026. A total of 3,352,161 ordinary shares were purchased at a volume weighted average price of 1,333p per share and subsequently cancelled. In the second half of the year, we established a £50m revolving credit facility which remained undrawn at the year-end date.

Regular meetings between senior representatives from sales, technology and vendor management teams to review technology and market trends and customer propositions

Continued investment in digital capabilities, technology development and strategic partnerships to address AI-driven customer and market shifts

Culture sits at the heart of all changes that are made in Softcat. There is regular communication from Senior Leadership Team members to employees at 'Kick Off' and 'all hands' calls about the importance of culture

The Group has taken a measured approach to the base case and has balanced expected trading conditions with the opportunities available to the business. The Group remains highly cash generative and maintains significant liquidity throughout the going concern period, with the existing RCF remaining undrawn.
>>>
